items.title: Ralph Sutton interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 22, 1995
items.q: We used to work, Gus and I used to work up in Billings, Montana in a hotel up there. Just the two of us.

ctx.x: It was hot huh? It was swinging?

Oh, man. It had that right tickin’ rhythm. Everybody was playing. The joint was jumping. And Gus Johnson on drums man. One of the greatest drummers I ever worked with. Really. He was right with it. We used to work, Gus and I used to work up in Billings, Montana in a hotel up there. Just the two of us. So I gave us the names of Frick and Frack. And we’d go up there for a four week engagement you know. Play six nights a week, off the seventh, so we’d be in somebody’s home. Gus would do the cooking and I’d make my…
Oh, great. Improvising in the kitchen.

I was out there with Ralph Sutton and (Franz Jackson -- ed.) -- oh, it's a guy called Franz, plays tenor, from Chicago. The other two guys, the bass player and trombone player, were from Minneapolis.
